_: The variant register. This file is the source of truth for index.html, the
portal that sits beside the variants — `npm run hub` reads it.
A VARIANT IS A FILE, NOT A BRANCH AND NOT A FOLDER. It is `indexN.html` in
this folder, published as-is, with its assets in `assetsN/`. That is the
naming every _buro test uses: _buro test 3 holds index1.html through
index20.html side by side, each with assets14/, assets16/, assets20/, and one
previews/indexN.jpg apiece. This project used to address variants as folders
on a separate gh-pages branch of a separate repository; that repository is
gone, and so is the branch. Files beside each other need neither.
Order is presentation order: newest first. `status` is free text and appears
on the card as written — 'current', 'superseded', 'experiment', a date, or
A variant is REMOVED by deleting its entry here, deleting its indexN.html and
A VARIANT IS A PAGE; A DIRECTION IS AN ART DIRECTION. index2/3/4.html are the
three directions explored off index1 — they share one bootstrap (src/site/vboot.js)
and differ only in src/directions/{a,b,c}.js and site/dir-{a,b,c}.css. The letter
survives inside the source because it names the direction; the published page is
still indexN.html, because that is the name the portal and the dashboard look for.
title: Machine study 01
subject: KUKA KR 700 PA

variants.name: Monumental
variants.note: Direction A. The machine as architecture — cropped on two or three edges in every shot, one hard source and almost no fill, and the callouts carrying the language in place of shot statements.

variants.name: Editorial
variants.note: Direction B. The machine as a printed subject: a measured column of type against a held frame, generous margins, the figures set as a plate rather than an overlay.

variants.name: Machine film
variants.note: Direction C. The machine as footage: long lens, shallow stops, the frame moving as a camera rather than as a page. Type stays out of the way of the shot.

variants.name: The level line
variants.note: Six camera stations around roughly 490° of travel. The datum lives in the room rather than on the glass, so the arm occludes it. Split-flap opening; instrument layer reads real azimuth and distance.
